words.enDefinition: a small discussion class where students present and debate readings

examples.en: In our Friday seminar, each student presents one chapter and then leads the debate.
examples.zh: 周五的「研讨课」上，每位学生讲一章内容，然后主持讨论。

examples.en: My seminar has only eight students, so hiding silently in the back row is impossible.
examples.zh: 我的「研讨课」只有八个学生，想安静地躲在后排根本不可能。

words.enDefinition: an informal discussion where everyone sits together as equals

examples.en: The department roundtable lets graduate students question senior professors about research ethics directly.
examples.zh: 系里的「圆桌讨论」让研究生能直接向资深教授提问科研伦理问题。

examples.en: At the careers roundtable, recent graduates shared how they landed their first interviews.
examples.zh: 在求职「圆桌讨论」上，刚毕业的学长学姐分享了拿到第一轮面试的经验。

words.enDefinition: several invited experts answering audience questions on a stage

examples.en: After each panel discussion, students line up at the microphone to ask one question.
examples.zh: 每场「嘉宾座谈」结束后，学生都排队到话筒前提一个问题。

examples.en: I was too nervous to speak at the panel discussion on AI and hiring.
examples.zh: 在那场关于人工智能与招聘的「嘉宾座谈」上，我紧张得没敢发言。

words.enDefinition: teaching where classes analyze real cases instead of hearing lectures

examples.en: Business school runs on the case study method, so you must prepare every case.
examples.zh: 商学院全靠「案例教学法」运转，所以每个案例都必须提前准备。

examples.en: Under the case study method, the professor cold-calls instead of lecturing from slides.
examples.zh: 在「案例教学法」的课堂上，教授不照幻灯片讲课，而是随机点名提问。

collocations: teach by the case study method
the case study method in business

words.enDefinition: teaching by probing questions until students can defend their reasoning

examples.en: Law professors use the Socratic method, questioning one student until the argument holds up.
examples.zh: 法学教授采用「苏格拉底问答法」，连续追问一个学生直到论证站得住脚。

examples.en: The Socratic method scared me at first, but it taught me to reason out loud.
examples.zh: 「苏格拉底问答法」起初让我害怕，但它教会我边说边推理。

words.enDefinition: practice court where law students argue appeals before judges

examples.en: Moot court gives law students practice arguing appeals in front of volunteer judges.
examples.zh: 「模拟法庭」让法学院学生在志愿法官面前练习上诉辩护。

examples.en: She joined the moot court team to get comfortable speaking under real pressure.
examples.zh: 她加入「模拟法庭」队，练习在真正的压力下发言。

words.enDefinition: an issue no longer worth discussing because it is settled

examples.en: Whether the old policy was fair is a moot point now that the deadline passed.
examples.zh: 旧政策是否公平已经是「无需再议的问题」，因为截止日期已过。

examples.en: He kept quoting the old rubric, but that is a moot point since the course moved online.
examples.zh: 他一直引用旧的评分标准，但课程已经改成线上，那已是「无需再议的问题」。

words.enDefinition: a regular department talk where researchers present current work

examples.en: The Friday colloquium is where visiting researchers present their latest work to the department.
examples.zh: 周五的「学术研讨会」是访问学者向全系展示最新成果的场合。

examples.en: Graduate students are expected to ask at least one question at every colloquium.
examples.zh: 研究生每场「学术研讨会」都至少要提一个问题。

words.enDefinition: a small informal group meeting regularly to discuss chosen texts

examples.en: Our reading group meets every Tuesday to argue about one paper over cheap coffee.
examples.zh: 我们的「读书会」每周二碰头，一边喝便宜咖啡一边争论一篇论文。

examples.en: The philosophy reading group welcomed me even though I had never taken the course.
examples.zh: 尽管我没修过那门课，哲学「读书会」还是欢迎我加入。

words.enDefinition: a regular meeting where students critically discuss recent papers

examples.en: In journal club, one member presents a recent paper and everyone else critiques it.
examples.zh: 在「文献研读会」上，一位成员讲解新论文，其余人负责点评。

examples.en: Presenting at journal club taught me how to question a study's methods politely.
examples.zh: 在「文献研读会」做展示教会了我如何礼貌地质疑研究方法。

words.enDefinition: to form pairs with nearby classmates for a quick task

examples.en: The TA told us to pair up and compare our reading responses for five minutes.
examples.zh: 助教让我们「两两分组」，花五分钟互相比较读书报告。

examples.en: Pair up with someone you have not spoken to yet in this seminar.
examples.zh: 和这门研讨课上还没说过话的同学「两人一组」吧。

words.enDefinition: an online forum where students post and reply on course topics

examples.en: Post your answer on the discussion board by Thursday and reply to two classmates.
examples.zh: 周四前把答案发到「课程讨论区」，并回复两位同学。

examples.en: The TA flagged my discussion board comment as a model reply for the class.
examples.zh: 助教把我在「课程讨论区」的评论标为全班范例回复。

words.enDefinition: a short written reply students upload for online discussion

examples.en: My discussion post earned full marks after I quoted one line and disagreed with it.
examples.zh: 我的「讨论帖」引用了原文一句话并提出异议，结果拿了满分。

examples.en: Write your discussion post before reading others' replies so your argument stays original.
examples.zh: 先写好自己的「讨论帖」再看别人的回复，这样观点才能保持原创。

words.enDefinition: prepared questions that guide what a class talks about

examples.en: The discussion leader emails three discussion questions the night before every seminar.
examples.zh: 每次研讨课前一晚，讨论主持人都会发来三道「讨论题」。

examples.en: I prepare answers to the discussion questions even for classes that never call on me.
examples.zh: 即使有些课从不点名，我也会提前准备「讨论题」的答案。

words.enDefinition: a short weekly write-up reacting to the assigned reading

examples.en: A weekly reading response of three hundred words keeps everyone honest about the reading.
examples.zh: 每周三百词的「每周读书报告」让谁都不敢不读材料。

examples.en: My TA said my weekly reading response should argue a position, not just summarize.
examples.zh: 助教说我的「每周读书报告」应当论证立场，而不是单纯总结。

words.enDefinition: to actually read assigned texts before class begins

examples.en: In a seminar you cannot hide, because everyone can tell who did the reading.
examples.zh: 研讨课上藏不住，谁都看得出谁「完成了课前阅读」。

examples.en: Doing the reading takes two hours, but facing a cold call unprepared is worse.
examples.zh: 「完成课前阅读」要花两小时，但没准备就被点名提问更糟糕。

words.enDefinition: careful line-by-line analysis of how a text works

examples.en: Our literature seminar spent forty minutes on a close reading of the opening paragraph.
examples.zh: 我们的文学课花了四十分钟，对开篇段落进行「文本细读」。

examples.en: Close reading pays off when the professor asks why the author chose that exact word.
examples.zh: 当教授追问作者为何偏用那个词时，你就知道「文本细读」的功夫没有白费。

collocations: a close reading of the passage

words.enDefinition: to add notes and questions in the margins while reading

examples.en: Annotate each article with one question so you have something ready when the discussion stalls.
examples.zh: 给每篇文章「批注」一个问题，讨论冷场时你就有的说了。

examples.en: She annotates every page, which makes finding quotes during seminar much faster.
examples.zh: 她每一页都「做批注」，因此研讨课上找引文快得多。

words.enDefinition: to read fast for main points, skipping the details

examples.en: Skimming the case before class is risky when the professor cold-calls on details.
examples.zh: 教授会就细节随机点名，所以课前只「略读」案例风险很大。

examples.en: If you are short on time, skim the introduction and the conclusion first.
examples.zh: 时间不够的话，先「略读」引言和结论部分。

words.enDefinition: to get materials and answers ready before a session

examples.en: I prep for class on the bus, rereading my notes and one highlighted quote.
examples.zh: 我在公交车上「做课前准备」，重读笔记和一条画了线的引文。

examples.en: The syllabus says to prep for class by writing two questions about the reading.
examples.zh: 课程大纲要求「课前准备」时写下两个关于阅读材料的问题。

collocations: prep for class the night before
prep for class with two questions

words.enDefinition: a portion of the grade based on how much you speak

examples.en: My participation grade is twenty percent, so staying silent all term is not an option.
examples.zh: 「课堂参与分」占两成，整学期保持沉默是行不通的。

examples.en: The TA explained that a good participation grade rewards quality comments, not constant talking.
examples.zh: 助教解释说，「课堂参与分」看重发言质量，而不是喋喋不休。

words.enDefinition: to be chosen by the teacher to answer in class

examples.en: My heart races whenever I get called on before I have finished thinking.
examples.zh: 每当还没想好就被「点到名」，我的心跳就狂飙。

examples.en: If you get called on without an answer, describe what you are still working through.
examples.zh: 如果被「点到名」却还没答案，就说说你正卡在哪一步。

collocations: get called on in every class

words.enDefinition: the frozen fear when a professor suddenly names you

examples.en: Cold-call panic fades once you learn to buy time with 'let me think aloud'.
examples.zh: 学会先说一句“容我边想边说”争取时间，「被点名的恐慌」就会消退。

examples.en: She manages her cold-call panic by keeping one prepared comment in her notes.
examples.zh: 她在笔记里常备一条观点，用来缓解「被点名时的慌乱」。

words.enDefinition: to force someone to answer immediately without preparation

examples.en: The professor put me on the spot by asking which author I found least convincing.
examples.zh: 教授当场问我觉得哪位作者最没说服力，简直「让人当场难堪」。

examples.en: Good TAs avoid putting shy students on the spot during the first few weeks.
examples.zh: 好的助教在开学头几周不会「逼害羞的学生当场回答」。

collocations: put a student on the spot
hate being put on the spot

words.enDefinition: to become confident enough to voice your own views

examples.en: Seminar discussions helped me find my voice after a term of sitting silently.
examples.zh: 沉默了一学期后，研讨课讨论帮我「找到了自己的声音」。

examples.en: Her TA encouraged her to find her voice by starting with short prepared comments.
examples.zh: 助教鼓励她从简短的准备性发言开始，「敢于发出自己的声音」。

collocations: find your voice in class discussions

words.enDefinition: to stop being withdrawn and start joining in

examples.en: Our discussion group is friendly enough for anyone to come out of their shell.
examples.zh: 我们的讨论小组氛围友好，谁都能「不再拘谨」。

examples.en: After two months of tutorials, he finally came out of his shell and argued back.
examples.zh: 上了两个月辅导课后，他终于「走出了自己的壳」，敢开口争论了。

collocations: come out of your shell gradually
help someone come out of their shell
finally come out of your shell

words.enDefinition: to gather courage slowly before doing something frightening

examples.en: It took me three weeks to work up the nerve to disagree with the professor.
examples.zh: 我花了三周才「鼓起勇气」反驳教授。

examples.en: I finally worked up the nerve to read my response aloud in front of everyone.
examples.zh: 我终于「鼓起勇气」，在全班面前朗读了我的读书回应。

collocations: work up the nerve to speak
work up the nerve to ask

words.enDefinition: to try something small first to gauge reactions

examples.en: Test the waters with one short comment before launching into a full argument.
examples.zh: 在抛出完整论证之前，先用一句简短发言「试探一下」。

examples.en: She tested the waters by asking a question instead of giving her whole opinion.
examples.zh: 她没有直接亮出完整观点，而是先提了个问题「试探反应」。

collocations: test the waters with a question
test the waters in a new class

words.enDefinition: to suddenly stop thinking or speaking because of nerves

examples.en: I froze up mid-sentence when the professor asked me to define the key term.
examples.zh: 教授让我定义那个核心概念时，我「卡壳」了，话说到一半停住。

examples.en: Even well-prepared students freeze up when the question comes out of nowhere.
examples.zh: 即使准备充分，学生遇到突袭式提问也会「僵住」。

collocations: freeze up during a cold call
freeze up in front of everyone

words.enDefinition: to lose your thoughts completely for a moment under pressure

examples.en: My mind went blank the moment the TA asked me to summarize the argument.
examples.zh: 助教让我总结论点的那一刻，我「大脑一片空白」。

examples.en: When your mind goes blank, repeat the question and buy yourself a few seconds.
examples.zh: 「大脑一片空白」时，先复述问题，给自己争取几秒钟。

words.enDefinition: starting to speak quickly, often before others finish

examples.en: Jumping in the moment someone pauses is normal in our seminar, not rude.
examples.zh: 在我们的研讨课上，别人一停顿就「抢着接话」很正常，不算失礼。

examples.en: She apologized for jumping in, but the pause had already lasted a full minute.
examples.zh: 她为「抢话」道歉，可那次停顿其实已经足足一分钟。

words.enDefinition: to add a short comment to an ongoing discussion

examples.en: Feel free to chime in with a quick example whenever the group gets abstract.
examples.zh: 每当讨论变得太抽象，欢迎随时「插话」补充一个具体例子。

examples.en: The quiet grad student chimed in once, and her point redirected the whole discussion.
examples.zh: 那位安静的研究生只「插了一句」，却让整场讨论换了方向。

words.enDefinition: to speak suddenly after staying quiet for a while

examples.en: Halfway through the debate, a first-year piped up with the sharpest question so far.
examples.zh: 辩论进行到一半，一个新生「突然开口」，问了至今最尖锐的问题。

examples.en: Nobody expects you to pipe up if you tell the TA beforehand that you are shy.
examples.zh: 如果你提前告诉助教你比较害羞，没人会指望你「突然发言」。

collocations: pipe up from the back row

words.enDefinition: to interrupt rudely without being invited into the talk

examples.en: Excuse me for butting in, but I think we are misreading the author's claim.
examples.zh: 原谅我「插嘴」，但我觉得我们误读了作者的观点。

examples.en: He kept butting in with jokes while the presenters were explaining their slides.
examples.zh: 展示的同学讲解幻灯片时，他不停「插嘴开玩笑」。

words.enDefinition: to keep speaking while another person is still talking

examples.en: The two presenters kept talking over each other until the moderator stepped in.
examples.zh: 两位展示者一直「盖过对方的说话声」，直到主持人出面才停。

examples.en: Talking over quieter classmates is the fastest way to lose goodwill in a seminar.
examples.zh: 在研讨课上「盖过安静同学的声头」，是败光好感的最快方式。

words.enDefinition: to manage to say something when others dominate the talk

examples.en: When one student hogs the discussion, nobody else can get a word in edgewise.
examples.zh: 一旦有人霸占讨论，别人就「一句话都插不上」。

examples.en: I finally got a word in edgewise after the TA called for shorter comments.
examples.zh: 助教呼吁发言简短之后，我终于「插上了一句话」。

collocations: can't get a word in edgewise
barely get a word in edgewise
finally get a word in edgewise

words.enDefinition: talking so much that others get no space to speak

examples.en: The TA emailed him privately about hogging the discussion in every single session.
examples.zh: 他每次课都「独占讨论」，助教私下发邮件提醒了他。

examples.en: Hogging the discussion feels productive, but it usually silences the quieter students.
examples.zh: 「霸占讨论」看似高产，通常却让安静的同学更不敢开口。

words.enDefinition: to talk at length in a confident, lecture-like way

examples.en: He held forth on Foucault for ten minutes until the TA politely cut in.
examples.zh: 他就福柯「高谈阔论」了十分钟，直到助教礼貌地打断。

examples.en: Our professor loves holding forth, so questions get pushed to the last five minutes.
examples.zh: 我们教授爱「长篇大论」，提问总是被挤到最后五分钟。

words.enDefinition: to talk in a long, disorganized way without a clear point

examples.en: I rambled for two minutes before the moderator gently asked what my main point was.
examples.zh: 我「东拉西扯」了两分钟，主持人才温和地问我的重点到底是什么。

examples.en: Ranting is rare in seminars, but rambling through an unprepared answer is common.
examples.zh: 研讨课上很少有人发火，但没准备时「说得漫无边际」很常见。

words.enDefinition: the share of speaking time each person takes in discussion

examples.en: The TA tracks airtime so the same three students do not dominate every debate.
examples.zh: 助教会记录「发言时间」，免得每次辩论都被同样三个人占满。

examples.en: I used to take up too much airtime without noticing I had the floor.
examples.zh: 我从前不知不觉「占用了太多发言时间」，自己却没察觉。

words.enDefinition: to add your opinion to a discussion already underway

examples.en: The professor usually waits ten minutes before weighing in with her own reading.
examples.zh: 教授通常先等十分钟，才「发表意见」说出自己的解读。

examples.en: Can I weigh in on the sampling question before we move to methodology?
examples.zh: 在进入方法论之前，我能就抽样问题「发表一下看法」吗？

words.enDefinition: your opinion offered modestly, as if it hardly matters

examples.en: Just my two cents, but the paper's conclusion overstates what the data shows.
examples.zh: 「一点浅见」，这篇论文的结论夸大了数据能支撑的范围。

examples.en: Can I offer my two cents on the debate question before we vote?
examples.zh: 表决之前，我能就这道辩题「说两点自己的浅见」吗？

words.enDefinition: to say honestly what you think, even if unpopular

examples.en: Seminars reward students who speak their mind politely, not those who stay safe.
examples.zh: 研讨课奖励的是「有礼有节说出真实想法」的学生，而不是明哲保身的人。

examples.en: It took a whole term before I felt free to speak my mind about the theory.
examples.zh: 过了整整一学期，我才敢对这套理论「畅所欲言」。

collocations: encourage students to speak their minds

words.enDefinition: to say something at the wrong moment or overstepping

examples.en: I worried I had spoken out of turn by challenging the guest speaker's data.
examples.zh: 我质疑了外请讲者的数据，担心自己「说话不合时宜」。

examples.en: The professor laughed it off and said nobody speaks out of turn in her class.
examples.zh: 教授一笑置之，说在她的课上不存在「说话失当」这回事。

collocations: speak out of turn in class
afraid of speaking out of turn

words.enDefinition: to hold back until it is your proper moment to speak

examples.en: Learn to wait your turn instead of cutting across whoever is speaking.
examples.zh: 要学会「等轮到自己再发言」，别打断正在说话的人。

examples.en: I waited my turn all class, and then time ran out before I spoke.
examples.zh: 我整节课都「等着轮到自己」，结果下课铃响前没轮上。

collocations: wait your turn in the discussion

words.enDefinition: someone who guides a group discussion without lecturing

examples.en: Each week one student acts as facilitator and keeps the group on the reading.
examples.zh: 每周由一名学生担任「讨论引导者」，让小组紧扣阅读材料。

examples.en: A good facilitator asks follow-up questions instead of offering her own conclusions.
examples.zh: 好的「引导者」会追问，而不是急着抛出自己的结论。

words.enDefinition: the person who runs a panel and manages questions and timing

examples.en: The moderator cut the debate short so every panelist could answer once more.
examples.zh: 「主持人」缩短了辩论时间，好让每位嘉宾再答一轮。

examples.en: As moderator, she redirected the panel whenever two speakers began attacking each other.
examples.zh: 身为「主持人」，每当嘉宾开始互相攻击，她就转移话题。

words.enDefinition: one of the invited speakers sitting on a panel

examples.en: Each panelist got two minutes to respond before the audience joined in.
examples.zh: 每位「座谈嘉宾」有两分钟回应时间，之后观众才能加入。

examples.en: One panelist admitted she had failed her first-year exams, which surprised everyone.
examples.zh: 一位「嘉宾」坦言自己大一挂过科，让所有人吃了一惊。

words.enDefinition: the group member who writes down the key points

examples.en: We rotate the note-taker so nobody gets stuck typing up the minutes every week.
examples.zh: 我们轮流当「记录员」，免得有人每周都倒霉负责整理纪要。

examples.en: The note-taker posted a summary of our breakout room before the class ended.
examples.zh: 下课前，「记录员」就把我们分组讨论的要点汇总发了出来。

words.enDefinition: the person chosen to present a group's conclusions

examples.en: Each breakout room picks a spokesperson to summarize its answer to everyone.
examples.zh: 每个分组讨论室推选一名「发言代表」，向全班总结答案。

examples.en: Nobody wanted to be spokesperson, so we drew lots and I lost.
examples.zh: 没人想当「发言代表」，我们抽签，结果抽中了我。

words.enDefinition: the student responsible for steering one week's discussion

examples.en: As discussion leader, I emailed two questions and opened the class with a short quote.
examples.zh: 担任「讨论主持人」时，我提前发了两个问题，并用一句短引文开场。

examples.en: Being discussion leader once a term pushes even shy students to prepare deeply.
examples.zh: 每学期轮值一次「讨论主持人」，再害羞的学生也得深入准备。

words.enDefinition: to manage a messy discussion and keep it productive

examples.en: The TA wrangled a discussion that kept sliding into complaints about the workload.
examples.zh: 讨论一再滑向对作业量的抱怨，助教费力地「驾驭着讨论」。

examples.en: Wrangling a discussion of twelve opinionated students is harder than it looks.
examples.zh: 「驾驭一场讨论」，让十二个主见十足的学生好好说话，比看上去难得多。

collocations: wrangle a discussion back on topic

words.enDefinition: to invite everyone present to start asking or commenting

examples.en: The professor opened the floor after twenty minutes of presentation and questions.
examples.zh: 讲授和提问二十分钟后，教授「开放了自由讨论」。

examples.en: Before we open the floor, let me answer the question about last week's rubric.
examples.zh: 在「开放自由发言」之前，先让我回答上周关于评分标准的问题。

words.enDefinition: to return to the main topic after drifting away

examples.en: The TA got us back on track by pointing at the week's second discussion question.
examples.zh: 助教指着本周第二道讨论题，把我们「拉回正题」。

examples.en: We kept drifting into housing costs until the facilitator got us back on track.
examples.zh: 我们一再聊到房租开销，直到引导者把我们「带回正题」。

collocations: get the discussion back on track
bring the class back on track

words.enDefinition: to start discussing something unrelated to the main topic

examples.en: Our sociology seminar went off on a tangent about campus parking for ten minutes.
examples.zh: 我们的社会学课「跑题」跑了十分钟，从论文一路聊到校园停车。

examples.en: It's easy to go off on a tangent when everyone starts sharing personal stories.
examples.zh: 大家一开始讲自己的经历，就很容易「扯远」。

collocations: go off on a tangent about
pull the class back from a tangent

words.enDefinition: to be drawn away from the planned topic by something else

examples.en: We got sidetracked comparing campuses and never reached the last discussion question.
examples.zh: 我们「聊偏了」，光顾着比较各个校园，最后一道讨论题没来得及。

examples.en: Groups get sidetracked easily when nobody keeps an eye on the clock.
examples.zh: 没人盯着时间的话，小组很容易「被带偏」。

words.enDefinition: a private chat between two people during a larger discussion

examples.en: The moderator paused and waited until every side conversation had died down completely.
examples.zh: 主持人停下不语，直到每场「开小会」都彻底安静下来。

examples.en: A side conversation about weekend plans kept pulling our attention away from the panel.
examples.zh: 旁边有人「开小会」聊周末计划，一直分散着我们听座谈的注意力。

words.enDefinition: to add to what a classmate said rather than starting over

examples.en: I'd like to build on Maria's point about stigma rather than start a new thread.
examples.zh: 我想「接着玛丽亚关于污名的观点」往下说，而不是另起话题。

examples.en: The best comments build on someone's point and push it one step further.
examples.zh: 最好的发言都是「顺着别人的观点」再推进一步。

words.enDefinition: to attach your idea to what someone just said

examples.en: Can I piggyback on that and add one counterexample from my own fieldwork?
examples.zh: 我可以「顺着这一点」补充一个我田野调查里的反例吗？

examples.en: She piggybacked on the previous comment to introduce her critique of the methodology.
examples.zh: 她「借着前一位的评论」，引出了自己对方法论的批评。

words.enDefinition: to notice a small remark and respond to it

examples.en: The professor picked up on my passing comment and turned it into the next debate.
examples.zh: 教授「接住了我随口一句话」，把它变成了下一轮辩论的题目。

examples.en: Pick up on what quieter classmates say; their brief notes often hide good questions.
examples.zh: 多「接话」安静同学说的内容，他们简短的笔记里常藏着好问题。

collocations: pick up on an earlier remark

words.enDefinition: to take someone's idea and develop it further yourself

examples.en: When the TA says run with an idea, she means develop it, not just repeat it.
examples.zh: 助教说「顺着想法展开」时，意思是深入发展它，而不是简单重复。

examples.en: The group ran with my half-formed idea and turned it into the final presentation.
examples.zh: 小组「顺着」我那个半成型的想法一路发展，做成了期末展示。

collocations: run with an idea from class
run with it for a while

words.enDefinition: to share half-formed ideas back and forth to improve them

examples.en: Before writing our responses, we bounce ideas off each other over cheap coffee.
examples.zh: 动笔写读书回应之前，我们先端着便宜咖啡「互相碰想法」。

examples.en: Brainstorming works best when you bounce ideas off each other without judging them too fast.
examples.zh: 「互相碰想法」又不过快评判时，头脑风暴效果最好。

collocations: bounce ideas off each other freely

words.enDefinition: a meeting where people generate as many ideas as possible

examples.en: Our brainstorming session produced twenty ideas, and we narrowed them to three after lunch.
examples.zh: 一场「头脑风暴」下来攒了二十个点子，午饭后收敛到三个。

examples.en: Save judgment for later; a brainstorming session falls apart the moment someone starts nitpicking.
examples.zh: 评价留到后面；一旦有人开始挑剔，「头脑风暴」就进行不下去了。

collocations: a brainstorming session for the essay

words.enDefinition: to suggest something casually to see if the group likes it

examples.en: Someone threw out an idea about debating the ethics code, and it stuck.
examples.zh: 有人「随口抛出一个想法」，要辩论伦理守则，结果被采纳了。

examples.en: Feel free to throw out an idea even if it sounds half-finished.
examples.zh: 哪怕想法听着半生不熟，也尽管「抛出来」。

collocations: throw out an idea for discussion

words.enDefinition: planned or thought out badly; not ready to use

examples.en: Seminars are the right place for half-baked ideas, because feedback turns them into arguments.
examples.zh: 研讨课恰恰欢迎「不成熟的想法」，同学反馈会把它们打磨成论证。

examples.en: My half-baked thesis got sharpened after the TA asked me two brutal questions.
examples.zh: 助教问了两个犀利的问题，我那个「半成型的论点」就被磨尖了。

words.enDefinition: to add details that make a basic idea complete

examples.en: The outline is solid, but you need to flesh out the middle section.
examples.zh: 大纲没问题，但中间部分还得「充实」一下。

examples.en: We fleshed out the two strongest proposals during the second breakout room.
examples.zh: 第二轮分组讨论时，我们把最强的两个方案「细化」了。

words.enDefinition: to say more about a point you or someone else made

examples.en: Could you expand on your second point about sample size and funding?
examples.zh: 关于样本量和经费的第二点，你能「再展开讲讲」吗？

examples.en: The professor asked her to expand on the connection she noticed between the two papers.
examples.zh: 教授请她「进一步展开」她发现的两篇论文之间的联系。

words.enDefinition: to explain a point more fully with added detail

examples.en: The TA asked me to elaborate instead of letting me stop at one sentence.
examples.zh: 助教让我「详细阐述」，没让我一句话就蒙混过关。

examples.en: Elaborate on your evidence before you attack the author's conclusion.
examples.zh: 在攻击作者结论之前，先把你的证据「阐述充分」。

words.enDefinition: to argue through disagreements until reaching a workable answer

examples.en: Our group hashed out the presentation split in twenty noisy minutes.
examples.zh: 小组吵吵嚷嚷二十分钟，总算「敲定」了展示分工。

examples.en: We stayed after class to hash out who would cover methodology and who would present.
examples.zh: 下课后我们留下来「商量定」，谁负责方法论、谁上台展示。

words.enDefinition: to restate someone's idea in your own simpler words

examples.en: Before you disagree, paraphrase the author's claim so the class knows you read it.
examples.zh: 反驳之前先「用自己的话复述」作者的主张，让全班知道你读过。

examples.en: She paraphrased the dense paragraph in two sentences and the whole group relaxed.
examples.zh: 她用两句话把那段艰深的段落「转述」出来，全组都松了口气。

words.enDefinition: to say the same thing again in different words

examples.en: Let me rephrase that, because I garbled the distinction between validity and soundness.
examples.zh: 让我「换个说法」，刚才我把有效性和可靠性的区别说乱了。

examples.en: If the question confuses people, the TA usually rephrases it with a concrete example.
examples.zh: 如果问题让大家困惑，助教通常会「换个说法」并配上具体例子。

words.enDefinition: a question with many possible answers rather than one

examples.en: Good discussion leaders favor open-ended questions that nobody can answer with a yes or no.
examples.zh: 高明的讨论主持人偏爱「开放式问题」，让人没法用是否作答。

examples.en: The TA replaced the quiz with one open-ended question about the week's reading.
examples.zh: 助教用一道关于本周阅读的「开放式问题」取代了小测。

collocations: an open-ended question about the reading

words.enDefinition: to ask a question, especially one worth discussing

examples.en: Each presenter must pose a question the rest of the seminar has to tackle.
examples.zh: 每位展示者都要「提出一个问题」，让研讨课其他人来攻克。

examples.en: She posed a question about ethics that kept our group talking past the deadline.
examples.zh: 她「抛出的伦理问题」让我们小组讨论得忘了截止时间。

collocations: pose a question to the class

words.enDefinition: summed up briefly in just a few words

examples.en: In a nutshell, the author argues that migration policy shaped the welfare state.
examples.zh: 「简而言之」，作者认为移民政策塑造了福利国家。

examples.en: Give us the article in a nutshell before we start pulling it apart.
examples.zh: 开始拆解之前，先「简而言之」概括一下文章大意。

words.enDefinition: used before defending someone or something against criticism

examples.en: To be fair, the study never claimed its sample represented the whole country.
examples.zh: 「说句公道话」，这项研究从未声称样本能代表全国。

examples.en: To be fair, the first-year presenter handled our toughest question better than expected.
examples.zh: 「平心而论」，这位大一展示者应对最刁钻问题的表现超出预期。

collocations: to be fair to the author

words.enDefinition: used to add a contrasting point after acknowledging something

examples.en: The method is elegant; that said, the sample is too small to generalize.
examples.zh: 这个方法很漂亮；「话虽如此」，样本太小，难以推广。

examples.en: I admire the theory. That said, applying it to our campus data seems forced.
examples.zh: 我欣赏这套理论，「尽管如此」，把它套在校内数据上仍显生硬。

collocations: that said, the evidence is thin

words.enDefinition: used to return to your point after an interruption

examples.en: As I was saying, the author's second claim depends on a much older dataset.
examples.zh: 「回到我刚才说的」，作者的第二个论点依赖一个旧得多的数据集。

examples.en: Sorry for the interruption; as I was saying, office hours moved to Thursday.
examples.zh: 抱歉刚才被打断；「接着刚才的话」，答疑时间改到周四了。

collocations: as I was saying before the interruption
return to as I was saying

words.enDefinition: Check whether a proposed reading is supported by the text or other evidence.

examples.en: We used the closing paragraph to test an interpretation that came up in the seminar.
examples.zh: 我们用最后一段来「检验一种解读」，这个解读是在研讨课上提出的。

examples.en: To test an interpretation, try explaining how it accounts for the change in the narrator's tone.
examples.zh: 要「检验一种解读」，可以试着解释它如何说明叙述者语气的改变。

collocations: test an interpretation against the evidence
test an interpretation of the passage
use a quotation to test an interpretation

words.enDefinition: a polite opener before disagreeing with someone senior

examples.en: With all due respect, Professor Hayes, the study contradicts the claim you just made.
examples.zh: 「恕我直言」，海斯教授，这项研究与您刚才的论断相矛盾。

examples.en: With all due respect to the panelist, her answer skipped the question entirely.
examples.zh: 「恕我冒昧」，这位嘉宾的回答完全绕开了问题本身。

collocations: with all due respect to the author
with all due respect, I disagree

words.enDefinition: to answer an argument against it firmly but respectfully

examples.en: Learn to rebut politely; disagreeing with the idea is not attacking the person.
examples.zh: 要学会「礼貌地反驳」：反对观点不等于攻击个人。

examples.en: She learned to rebut politely, citing two studies the panel had ignored.
examples.zh: 她学会了「有礼有节地反驳」，引用了两场座谈被忽视的研究。

words.enDefinition: a response that argues against what someone else claimed

examples.en: Her rebuttal quoted the dataset the original presenter had conveniently skipped.
examples.zh: 她的「反驳」引用了原展示者恰好略过的数据集。

examples.en: Keep your rebuttal short: one concession, one objection, one piece of evidence.
examples.zh: 「反驳」要短：一个让步、一个异议、一条证据。

words.enDefinition: an opposing argument raised against a claim or proposal

examples.en: The strongest counterargument came from the student who had just presented in favor.
examples.zh: 最有力的「反方论点」恰恰来自刚做完支持方展示的学生。

examples.en: Anticipate the obvious counterargument, or the professor will raise it for you.
examples.zh: 要预判显而易见的「反驳论点」，否则教授会替你提出来。

words.enDefinition: a contrasting view offered to balance someone's argument

examples.en: Let me offer a counterpoint from the employers' side of the debate.
examples.zh: 请允许我从辩论中雇主一方提出一个「对立观点」。

examples.en: Every counterpoint he raised made the presenter refine her claim instead of defending it blindly.
examples.zh: 他提出的每个「相反观点」都促使展示者打磨论断，而不是盲目辩护。

words.enDefinition: to disagree strongly and say so openly

examples.en: I take issue with the sampling method, not with the authors' overall goal.
examples.zh: 我对抽样方法「持异议」，并非针对作者的总体目标。

examples.en: She took issue with the way the TA framed the migration question.
examples.zh: 她对助教提出移民问题的方式「表示异议」。

words.enDefinition: to prove that a statement or argument is wrong

examples.en: One archival email refuted the claim the whole seminar had accepted.
examples.zh: 一封档案邮件就「驳倒」了全研讨课都接受的论断。

examples.en: You cannot refute a study by disliking it; show where the data breaks.
examples.zh: 你不喜欢一项研究并不能「驳倒」它，得指出数据究竟哪里有问题。

collocations: refute the argument point by point

words.enDefinition: to find weak spots that make an argument unreliable

examples.en: The professor poked holes in my methodology until I finally saw the confound.
examples.zh: 教授不断「挑我方法论上的毛病」，直到我终于看清那个混淆变量。

examples.en: We spent the seminar poking holes in a famous study that later failed replication.
examples.zh: 整节研讨课我们都在给那项著名研究「找漏洞」，它后来果然未能重复验证。

words.enDefinition: an exaggerated version of an argument, easy to attack

examples.en: Calling the theory useless is a straw man; the paper never claimed that much.
examples.zh: 说这套理论一无是处是「稻草人谬误」，原论文可没夸下这么大的海口。

examples.en: The TA showed us how a straw man hides the real disagreement between the two authors.
examples.zh: 助教向我们演示了「稻草人论证」如何掩盖两位作者真正的分歧。

words.enDefinition: a common reasoning error that makes an argument invalid

examples.en: The TA walked us through each fallacy in the editorial, from false dilemma to slippery slope.
examples.zh: 助教带我们逐一指出社论里的「逻辑谬误」，从虚假两难到滑坡谬误。

examples.en: Name the fallacy calmly; calling someone illogical never wins a seminar debate.
examples.zh: 冷静指出「谬误」何在；骂人不讲逻辑赢不下研讨课辩论。

words.enDefinition: arguing the opposite side on purpose to test the group's thinking

examples.en: The professor was just playing devil's advocate; she actually agreed with our critique.
examples.zh: 教授只是在「故意唱反调」，其实她认同我们的批评。

examples.en: Playing devil's advocate is easier than defending a position you truly hold.
examples.zh: 「故意唱反调」比捍卫你真心持有的立场要容易。

collocations: play devil's advocate to test an idea

words.enDefinition: to present reasons supporting a position or proposal

examples.en: Your response paper should make a case for one interpretation, not list three.
examples.zh: 你的回应论文应当「为一种解读进行论证」，而不是罗列三种。

examples.en: He made a case for extending the deadline by citing the campus outage.
examples.zh: 他举出校园断网一事，「为延长期限提出了充分理由」。

words.enDefinition: to state clearly which side or position you support

examples.en: The rubric rewards students who take a stance early and defend it with evidence.
examples.zh: 评分标准青睐早早「亮明立场」并用证据捍卫的学生。

examples.en: I used to sit on the fence, but the TA pushed me to take a stance.
examples.zh: 我从前不表态，助教推着我必须「选定立场」。

collocations: take a stance on the issue

words.enDefinition: to avoid saying which side you support in a debate

examples.en: Sitting on the fence protects you in some classrooms but looks evasive here.
examples.zh: 在某些课堂里「不表态」是自我保护，在这里却显得回避。

examples.en: The professor called on me precisely because I was sitting on the fence again.
examples.zh: 教授偏偏点我，正因为我又一次「骑墙不表态」。

collocations: sit on the fence during debates
accused of sitting on the fence

words.enDefinition: shared opinions that opposing sides can agree on first

examples.en: Start from common ground before you challenge the author's central claim.
examples.zh: 先从「共同立场」出发，再去挑战作者的核心论断。

examples.en: After an hour of arguing, both sides found common ground on the second question.
examples.zh: 争论一小时后，双方在第二个问题上找到了「共同点」。

collocations: common ground between the two camps

words.enDefinition: to end a disagreement politely while keeping different opinions

examples.en: After forty minutes, the seminar agreed to disagree on the definition of agency.
examples.zh: 争论四十分钟后，全班就“能动性”的定义「各自保留意见」。

examples.en: Sometimes you agree to disagree and spend the remaining time on the next question.
examples.zh: 有时只能「求同存异」，把剩下的时间留给下一个问题。

collocations: agree to disagree and move on

words.enDefinition: to fully agree with someone about something

examples.en: My lab partner and I never see eye to eye on how to frame the introduction.
examples.zh: 我和实验搭档在引言怎么写上从来「看法不一致」。

examples.en: Once she explained her dataset, we finally saw eye to eye on the method.
examples.zh: 等她讲清数据集，我们终于在这一方法上「意见一致」。

collocations: see eye to eye on policy
see eye to eye with someone

words.enDefinition: sharing the same understanding or plan as others

examples.en: Before the presentation, our group met to make sure everyone was on the same page.
examples.zh: 展示前我们开了个短会，确保每个人「想法一致」。

examples.en: The TA checked that we were all on the same page about the new rubric.
examples.zh: 助教确认我们对新的评分标准「理解一致」。

collocations: get everyone on the same page
on the same page about deadlines
keep the group on the same page

words.enDefinition: to explain clearly how two similar things differ

examples.en: The professor drew a distinction between correlation and causation before we analyzed the data.
examples.zh: 看数据之前，教授先在相关与因果之间「作出了区分」。

examples.en: Draw a distinction between the author's claims and the media's summary of them.
examples.zh: 要把作者的主张和媒体的概括「区分开来」。

words.enDefinition: to wrongly merge two different ideas into one

examples.en: The editorial conflates correlation with cause, which the seminar spent an hour untangling.
examples.zh: 这篇社论把相关「混同于」因果，研讨课花了一小时才理清。

examples.en: Do not conflate the author's personal views with the narrator's voice in the novel.
examples.zh: 别把作者本人的观点和小说叙述者的声音「混为一谈」。

words.enDefinition: a small but important difference in meaning or quality

examples.en: The TA pushed us to capture the nuance between tolerance and indifference.
examples.zh: 助教要求我们抓住宽容与冷漠之间的「细微差别」。

examples.en: Her comment added nuance to a debate that had turned too binary.
examples.zh: 她的发言让这场变得非黑即白的辩论多了一层「微妙差异」。

words.enDefinition: an example that disproves or weakens a general claim

examples.en: One counterexample from Japan weakened the professor's sweeping claim about exam culture.
examples.zh: 一个来自日本的「反例」动摇了教授关于考试文化的笼统论断。

examples.en: A good counterexample forces the presenter to narrow the claim instead of abandoning it.
examples.zh: 一个好的「反例」会促使展示者收窄论断，而非全盘放弃。

words.enDefinition: based on personal stories rather than systematic evidence

examples.en: My roommate's story is anecdotal, so do not build your whole argument on it.
examples.zh: 我室友的例子只是「个人见闻」，别把整个论证都押在上面。

examples.en: The presenter admitted her evidence was anecdotal and promised a survey next term.
examples.zh: 展示者承认她的证据只是「道听途说」，并承诺下学期做问卷调查。

words.enDefinition: based on observation, measurement, or data rather than theory

examples.en: The seminar wants empirical support, not just a clever reading of the theory.
examples.zh: 研讨课要的是「实证」支撑，而不只是对理论的机巧解读。

examples.en: Her empirical evidence came from two years of classroom observation data.
examples.zh: 她的「实证」证据来自两年的课堂观察数据。

words.enDefinition: your immediate feeling about something before careful thought

examples.en: Share your gut reaction first, then we will test it against the evidence.
examples.zh: 先说说你的「直觉反应」，我们再用证据来检验。

examples.en: My gut reaction was that the ending felt dishonest, and the seminar agreed.
examples.zh: 我的「第一反应」是结局显得不真诚，研讨课上大家也这么觉得。

collocations: a gut reaction to the text

words.enDefinition: a bold instant opinion shared without much evidence

examples.en: Hot takes get laughs in seminar, but the TA wants claims you can defend.
examples.zh: 「武断快评」能在研讨课上博得一笑，但助教要的是站得住的主张。

examples.en: Sorry for the hot take about the film; let me back it up with the text.
examples.zh: 抱歉刚才对电影下了个「武断的快评」，让我用原文把它撑起来。

collocations: a hot take on the reading

words.enDefinition: a prepared idea you plan to raise in discussion

examples.en: I keep three talking points on an index card in case my nerves hit.
examples.zh: 我在索引卡上备好三条「发言要点」，以防临场紧张。

examples.en: Her talking points covered the paper's method, sample, and one missing variable.
examples.zh: 她的「论点要点」覆盖了论文的方法、样本和一个遗漏变量。

words.enDefinition: a careful judgment of a work's strengths and weaknesses

examples.en: Our TA models a good critique: one strength, one weakness, one suggestion.
examples.zh: 我们的助教示范了何为好的「点评」：一个优点、一个不足、一条建议。

examples.en: The professor gave my presentation a blunt critique without ever making it personal.
examples.zh: 教授对我的展示给出了直率的「批评」，却始终对事不对人。

words.enDefinition: to separate tangled ideas or causes to see each clearly

examples.en: The seminar teased apart three different meanings of 'freedom' in the text.
examples.zh: 研讨课把文本中“自由”的三层含义逐一「梳理辨析」。

examples.en: Tease apart the two claims before deciding whether they actually conflict.
examples.zh: 先「拆解辨析」这两个论断，再判断它们是否真的冲突。

words.enDefinition: a talk several students prepare and deliver together

examples.en: Our group presentation ran eight minutes over because nobody timed the Q&A part.
examples.zh: 我们的「小组展示」超时八分钟，因为没人掐问答环节的表。

examples.en: The rubric grades the group presentation on clarity, timing, and handling questions.
examples.zh: 评分标准从清晰度、时间和应对提问三方面给「小组展示」打分。

words.enDefinition: to split a shared task into parts each member handles

examples.en: We divided up the work by strengths: slides, sources, and delivery.
examples.zh: 我们按各自长处「分工」：幻灯片、资料检索和现场讲述。

examples.en: Divide up the work on day one, or two people will do everything later.
examples.zh: 第一天就「分好工」，不然到后面就成了两个人干所有活。

collocations: divide up the slides and research

words.enDefinition: to do your fair share of a group's work

examples.en: Group projects work when everyone pulls their weight and says so honestly.
examples.zh: 只要人人都「尽了本分」且坦诚沟通，小组作业就会顺利。

examples.en: He finally pulled his weight after the TA asked each member to list contributions.
examples.zh: 助教要求每人列出贡献清单后，他总算「出了自己该出的力」。

collocations: pull your weight in a group

words.enDefinition: a group member who shares the grade but not the work

examples.en: Every group has one free rider who disappears until the day of the presentation.
examples.zh: 每个小组都有一名「搭便车的」，直到展示当天才现身。

examples.en: Our TA lets members report free riders, which lowers that person's individual score.
examples.zh: 我们的助教允许组员举报「不出力蹭分的人」，这会拉低其个人分数。

collocations: a free rider in the group

words.enDefinition: to return to the class and share your group's results

examples.en: Each breakout room has five minutes to report back with one sentence.
examples.zh: 每个分组讨论室有五分钟「汇报」，只用一句话概括。

examples.en: When we reported back, the moderator wrote our three ideas on the shared screen.
examples.zh: 我们「汇报结果」时，主持人把我们组的三个想法写上了共享屏幕。

words.expression: ground your argument in the text
words.lemma: ground your argument in the text
words.enDefinition: to support your argument with evidence from the material being discussed
acceptedEnVariants: ground your argument in the text

examples.en: You can ground your argument in the text by quoting the final paragraph.
examples.zh: 你可以引用最后一段，「以原文为依据论证」。

examples.en: The seminar guide says to ground your argument in the text during the debate.
examples.zh: 导师要求辩论时要「以原文为依据论证」。

collocations: ground your argument in the text itself
ground your argument in the text with a quotation
try to ground your argument in the text
